All four explorers have returned and I verified the load-bearing claims directly. Here is the audit.

---

# Audit: porting a receipt-bound multi-model Wizard onto current main

Bottom line: do not port the old Wizard. Every contract it needs already exists on current main. Build a bounded single-model proof-of-concept as a plugin flow first, then widen to three seats. The baseline has two real defects (lockfile drift and a missing dependency) plus one boundary gap (provider SDK code in `core/flowmind`), none of which block the POC but all of which must be named in its receipts.

All paths are relative to the worktree root. Claims marked "inference" were not directly observed.

## 1. Contracts the Wizard should reuse (verified by read)

Invocation truth (core/exec, core/domain):

- `createExec` — `core/exec/src/index.ts:69` — the blessed execution factory; emits `exec.started/completed/failed` and captures `durationMs` per call.
- `resolveExecutionBinding` — `core/exec/src/execution/execution-binding.ts:1152` — resolves a request to an `ExecutionBinding` (`:57`, schema `execution-binding.v1`).
- `ExecutionBindingSelectionProvenance.model_provenance` — `execution-binding.ts:117` — the literal requested-versus-resolved-model contract: `{ requested, resolved, alias_applied, source, row_id_format }`. This is the exact seam the Wizard needs; do not invent another.
- `resolveModelRoute` + `ModelRoutePurpose` (includes `judge`, `review`, `research`) — `core/exec/src/providers/model-router.ts:214` and `:7-19` — a ready fan-out router for N models.
- `executeTransportNode` / `ExecutionNodeResult` — `core/exec/src/execution/transport.ts:107` and `:34-47` — raw output capture: `output`, `outputPath`, `stdoutPath`, `stderrPath`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`. Raw output is carried as `LogRef`-style evidence pointers, not a domain "rawOutput" field.
- `TokenUsage` — `core/domain/src/usage.ts:33` — per-invocation `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `costUSD`, `usageSource`, `confidence`, `raw`; per-provider mappers and `mergeTokenUsageByModel` in `core/exec/src/providers/usage-mapper.ts`.
- `AgentPort` — `core/domain/src/agent-port.ts:21` — the provider-neutral agent port; `AgentPortResult.tokenUsageByModel` (`:106`). Note it is not in the domain index barrel; import by subpath.
- `RunLedgerWriter` port — `core/domain/src/run-fabric.ts:775` (admit/append/claim/seal); implemented by `RunService` in `core/execution-ledger/src/index.ts:28-36`. There is no `core/runs` package; the ledger is `core/execution-ledger`. Only exec writes it, via `recordExecRunSeal` — `core/exec/src/run/ledger-writer.ts:64`.
- `InvocationEvidenceRecord` — `core/exec/src/handlers/invocation-evidence-record.ts:48` — the sealed exec receipt; `PersistExecInvocationEvidenceRecordParams` (`core/exec/src/handlers/exec-receipt-types.ts:1`) already carries `tokenUsage` into the seal.

Measurement without verdicts (core/eval, core/domain):

- `Measurement` / `VariableTriple` / `MeasurementProvenance` — `core/domain/src/run-fabric.ts:80-95, :70-74, :76-78` — `lev.measurement.v1`, carries no pass/fail.
- `FileMeasurementStreamWriter` / `parseMeasurementJsonl` — `core/eval/src/measurement-stream.ts:12-54`.
- The adapters enforce the projection rule mechanically: `worldModelEvidenceToMeasurement` rejects any input bearing `verdict`, `gate_proof`, `proof_bundle`, `effect_receipt`, or `run_seal` fields with reason `truth_minting` unless it is marked `non_authoritative_input` with `load_bearing: false` — `core/eval/src/world-model-evidence-adapter.ts:4-10, :59-65`; same pattern in `sim-witness-provider-evidence-adapter.ts:16-43`. A Wizard measurement adapter must copy this shape.

Gate decision, kept separate:

- `discharge` — `core/eval/src/discharge.ts:35-134` — compares measurements against a `GatePolicy` (`run-fabric.ts:184-192`); missing or stale variables produce `evaluation_error`, fail closed.
- `dischargeEvalDecision` / `isEvalDecision` — `core/eval/src/eval-decision.ts:72-116, :118-134` — the guard actively rejects objects carrying dissolved scorecard fields (`:55-70`), which is the enforced Score-versus-Verdict split.
- Advisory enforcement of model output: `evaluatorEnforcement` — `core/eval/src/invocation-receipt.ts:100-115` — non-blocking evaluators project as `{mode:'advisory', blocking:false}`. Model prose enters as advisory evidence here, never as a verdict.

Proof and replay:

- `ProofBundle` (`lev.proof_bundle.v1`) — `run-fabric.ts:662-673`; `ReplayPacket` — `:650-660`; `assembleProofBundle` — `core/eval/src/proof-bundle.ts:103-129`; `validateProofRunEvidence` — `:253-362` — the replay-grade gate that requires receipt, trace, decided decisions, verifier command output, and durable refs, and forbids ephemeral `codex-tool-output://` refs.
- Replayable eval bundle: `EvalRun` — `core/eval/src/suite-runner.ts:59-72` — persists `run.json`, `measurements.jsonl`, `decision.json`, `seal.json` under the XDG execution-ledger root. Evaluator packs load from `plugins/*/evals` (`core/eval/src/evaluator-pack-loader.ts:61-68`) — the Wizard's evals live in its plugin, not in core.
- Multi-model budget gate already exists: `BestOfNRolloutPolicy` (rollout count 2 to 8, `budgetUsd`, `maxConcurrency`) — `core/eval/src/index.ts:128-132`, `core/eval/src/strategy/`.

Composition (core/flowmind, plugins):

- Graph IR ensemble fields — `core/domain/src/graph/types.ts:122-127, :159-163` — `targets`, `concurrency`, `failure_mode: all|any|majority`, `sync_mode: majority_complete`, `diversity_lens`; executed by `core/flowmind/src/graph-parallel-node.ts`. This is the native "council" substrate; note no plugin flow currently exercises it (inference from explorer sweep).
- Live deliberation exemplar: `plugins/cdo/flows/cdo-adaptive-deliberation.flow.yaml` — agent dispatch bound from a profile's `provider_binding` (`:107-122`), synthesis with `required_gate_proof_refs` (`:124-142`), receipts via `op: lev.receipts.append` (`:169-204`). Seat policy in `plugins/cdo/profiles/parliament.yaml` (bounds, dissent rules, `provider_binding` at `:33-36`).
- `plugins/samurai` is not a council. It is a graph-walker exemplar (router flow, subflow calls, `op: lev.exec`, receipt emission in `plugins/samurai/flows/samurai.flow.yaml:68-125, :215-249`). Useful as a flow-authoring template only.

## 2. Where provider implementations may live, and where they are forbidden

Allowed — `plugins/platforms`, the declared provider island (`plugins/platforms/dna/provider-boundary.yaml:22-27`):

- SDK adapters: `plugins/platforms/src/adapters/ai-sdk-provider.ts:1-3` (`@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/cerebras`) and `claude-agent-sdk.ts:1` — note this lane is marked deprecated (`:3-9`).
- Declarative provider cards: `plugins/platforms/providers/{claude-code,claude-code-print,codex,cursor-agent,opencode,pi,agy,shell-proof}/card.yaml`, guarded by `plugins/platforms/tests/provider-card-roots.test.ts`.
- Model catalogs: `plugins/platforms/src/model-catalog/`.

Forbidden — verified directly:

- `core/exec/tests/boundary-audit-rules.ts:455-467` — rule `no_provider_implementation_in_core`, severity hard, bans `@ai-sdk|@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk|@lev-os/platforms|generateText|streamText|query(` — but its `files` scope is `['core/exec/src', 'core/exec/src']` only.
- Inter-core edges: `tooling/scripts/validate-core-boundary-imports.mjs` derived from `dna/architecture/core-boundaries/concept.yaml:118-135`.
- Provider history paths banned in harness/orchestration: `tooling/scripts/runtime-lockdown-guard-lib.mjs:91-104`.

Known gap (verified): `core/flowmind/src/ai-provider.ts:11` imports `generateText, embedMany` from `ai` and dynamically imports `@ai-sdk/openai` (`:77`) and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (`:81`). This is real provider implementation inside core that the exec-scoped rule does not scan and the DNA allowlist does not cover (flowmind has no `tier_import_allowlist` entry). Treat it as a legacy seam, not a licence: the Wizard must not import it, extend it, or copy the pattern.

## 3. Smallest honest vertical slice

One plugin, one flow, one seat, one real model. Everything below is composition of existing symbols; no new core code.

1. Author `plugins/<name>/flows/<name>-seat.flow.yaml` (samurai/cdo idiom): one agent node whose `inputs.adapter/model/variant` come from a profile `provider_binding` (copy `plugins/cdo/profiles/parliament.yaml:33-36`), dispatched through `op: lev.exec`.
2. Binding truth: the request resolves through `resolveExecutionBinding` so the sealed receipt carries `model_provenance { requested, resolved, alias_applied }` from a real provider card (for example `plugins/platforms/providers/claude-code-print/card.yaml`).
3. Invocation truth: `executeTransportNode` captures `outputPath`, `stdoutPath`, `stderrPath`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`; the usage mapper produces `TokenUsage` including `costUSD`; the seal path is `recordExecRunSeal` → `RunService.seal` → `RunSeal` (`lev.run_seal.v1`) plus an `InvocationEvidenceRecord` with `tokenUsage`.
4. Measurement projection: a small adapter in the plugin converts the raw output into a `Measurement` with `status: 'non_authoritative_input'`-style provenance, written via `FileMeasurementStreamWriter`, copying the forbidden-field rejection from `world-model-evidence-adapter.ts:4-10`. No verdict fields anywhere in this stage.
5. Gate decision, separately: `discharge()` against a `GatePolicy` over mechanical variables only — exit code zero, output artifact present, token usage captured, model_provenance complete. The model's prose contributes nothing to the verdict.
6. Proof bundle: persist via the `EvalRun` artifact layout, then `assembleProofBundle` and prove it with `validateProofRunEvidence`, including a `ReplayRef`.

Tests for the slice:

- A receipt-binding test: the sealed record's `model_provenance.requested` differs-or-matches `resolved` as expected for an alias (for example `opus` → concrete id), and `selection_provenance` is present (guard: `core/domain/src/authority.ts:49, :484-486`).
- A projection-purity test: `measurements.jsonl` parses via `parseMeasurementJsonl` and contains no `verdict`, `gate_proof`, `proof_bundle`, `effect_receipt`, or `run_seal` fields.
- A false-green test: `validateProofRunEvidence` fails when the trace ref or verifier output is removed (the existing negative-path style in `core/eval/src/__tests__/false-green.test.ts`).
- The existing repo-wide boundary inventory stays at zero violations (`core/exec/tests/boundary-audit.test.ts:952-969`).

Only after this seals cleanly, widen to three seats — either three `provider_binding` profiles in a cdo-style round/synthesis flow, or the graph IR parallel node with `sync_mode: majority_complete` and `diversity_lens`. The parallel-node route is unproven at plugin layer today; the cdo route is live. Both remain admissible — decide after the single-seat slice, on evidence.

## 4. Triage of the old Wizard idea

- Already domain semantics on main (reuse, port nothing): receipt binding, requested/resolved model, token/cost/timing provenance, evidence refs, replay packets, measurement-versus-verdict separation. The old Wizard's "receipt-bound" core is now the platform's native vocabulary.
- Belongs in FlowMind/plugin composition: council topology (seats, rounds, dissent, synthesis), seat-to-model binding, prompts, budgets, evaluator packs. Home: a plugin with flows plus profiles, following cdo; evals under `plugins/<name>/evals` per the pack loader roots.
- Should not be ported: direct provider lanes (SDK calls inside Wizard code — forbidden in core, and the SDK lane in plugins/platforms is itself deprecated in favour of card-driven CLI transport); Wizard-minted verdicts from model prose; any bespoke receipt format; and the name itself — "wizard" already means CLI onboarding on main (`core/poly/src/commands/wizard.ts`, `core/build/src/wizard/runner.ts`, `core/onboarding/src/wizard.ts`). One word, one meaning: pick a new name (council, parliament, or extend cdo).

## 5. Baseline verdict (question 5)

The reported `core/exec` failure is a build-order requirement, not a code defect and not lockfile drift. Evidence: `core/exec` typecheck passes now (I ran `tsc --noEmit`, exit 0). `--traceResolution` shows `@lev-os/flowmind/exec-flow-validation` resolving through node_modules exports to `core/flowmind/dist/exec-flow-validation.d.ts` — the tsconfig wildcard mapping (`core/exec/tsconfig.json:38-40` → `../flowmind/src/*`) produces an extensionless target that NodeNext rejects, so resolution falls back to the exports map, whose `types` point at dist (`core/flowmind/package.json:40-44`, `core/config/package.json:44-48`). Both source modules and exports entries exist and are correct. The dist artifacts were built tonight (23:13 and 23:23 on 9 July — file timestamps), which is why the error no longer reproduces. Conclusion (inference, strongly supported): typecheck of core/exec before building `@lev-os/flowmind` and `@lev-os/config` reports exactly those two unresolved declarations; after `pnpm -r build` (or building those two), it passes.

However, the baseline is not otherwise clean. Two genuine committed defects, plus worktree contamination:

- Lockfile drift (committed): `core/event-providers/package.json:20` declares `@lev-os/config: workspace:*` but the committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` importer block for `core/event-providers` (around line 1406) omits it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` would fail; a plain install rewrites the lockfile, which is exactly the uncommitted 6-line lockfile diff sitting in the worktree.
- Missing declared dependency (committed code defect): `core/workstream/src/state.ts:14`, `src/adapters/filesystem.ts:12`, and `src/validators/workstream-shape.ts:17` import `@lev-os/config/source-catalog`, but the committed `core/workstream/package.json` does not declare `@lev-os/config`. The uncommitted local edit adds it.
- The worktree is therefore not clean: `core/workstream/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` carry uncommitted edits. Per instructions I fixed nothing.

## 6. No-go list and recommendation

No-go:

1. No provider SDK imports in any core package; do not touch or extend `core/flowmind/src/ai-provider.ts`.
2. No new spawn/exec paths — all invocation through `core/exec` transports and provider cards (GATE A3 in the boundary gate).
3. No verdicts minted from model prose; verdicts only via `core/eval` discharge; measurement adapters must reject verdict-bearing input as truth minting.
4. No merged Score/Verdict result type (`isEvalDecision` enforces this).
5. No bespoke receipt or proof formats — `lev.run_seal.v1`, `lev.proof_bundle.v1`, `InvocationEvidenceRecord` only.
6. No ledger writes except through exec's ledger writer.
7. No wholesale port of the old subtree, no "wizard" name in core, and no proof-gate asset with a merge/last-wins collision policy.

Recommendation: bounded POC now, full port never. The receipt, binding, measurement, and proof contracts on main are complete and stronger than anything the old branch could carry over, and cdo proves the deliberation shape end to end. What is unproven is the specific composition — a plugin flow that binds one real model and survives `validateProofRunEvidence` — and the parallel-node ensemble path has no live plugin proof at all. Build the single-seat slice in section 3 first; its seal is the evidence that decides the three-council step. Before or alongside it, the two committed baseline defects (event-providers lockfile drift, workstream missing dependency) should be fixed by whoever owns main, and the flowmind provider leak should get a boundary-rule scope extension — otherwise the Wizard POC's green CI sits on a baseline that cannot install frozen.

Uncertainties and limits: I could not observe the original failing typecheck invocation, so the build-order classification is inference from resolution traces and timestamps, not a reproduction. Line numbers in sections 1, 2, and 4 largely come from four read-only explorer agents; I independently re-verified the two load-bearing citations (the provider-ban rule scope at `boundary-audit-rules.ts:455-467` and the flowmind SDK imports) but not every line individually. No tests or builds were run, only `tsc --noEmit`. I have no visibility into the old Lev branch itself; the do-not-port judgments are calibrated against current main's contracts only.
